title: Skyroot Aerospace Set to Launch India's First Private Orbital Rocket Vikram-1 on July 18
excerpt: India is about to make space history. Skyroot Aerospace, the Hyderabadbased startup that became the country's first spacetech unicorn earlier this year, is set to launch its Vikram1 rocket from Sriharikota on July 18…
body:
India is about to make space history. Skyroot Aerospace, the Hyderabad-based startup that became the country's first spacetech unicorn earlier this year, is set to launch its Vikram-1 rocket from Sriharikota on July 18 at 11:30 am — marking the first time a private Indian company attempts an orbital-class launch.

## Mission Aagaman: A New Chapter for Indian Space

The mission, christened Mission Aagaman (meaning "arrival"), will carry technology demonstration payloads from Grahaa Space, Cosmoserve, DCubed, and Skyroot's own SCOPE instrument, along with an artwork piece called "Cosmic Bloom" by Cosmos Diamonds.

Vikram-1 is a seven-storey-tall, multi-stage launch vehicle built with an all-carbon composite structure and 3D-printed engines. It is designed to carry small satellites weighing up to 350 kg into Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

"We have done everything that could be done to test Vikram-1 on the ground. On 18 July, we are eager to see how Vikram-1 performs in a real flight environment for the first time," said CEO Pawan Kumar Chandana.

## From ISRO Labs to Billion-Dollar Valuation

Founded in 2018 by former ISRO scientists Pawan Kumar Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka, Skyroot has risen rapidly through India's burgeoning private space sector. The company raised $60 million in May 2026 in a round co-led by Sherpalo Ventures and Singapore's GIC, along with approximately $10 million in structured debt from BlackRock-affiliated funds.

The investment valued the company at $1.1 billion on a pre-money basis — making it India's first spacetech unicorn. Ram Shriram, founder of Sherpalo Ventures and an early Google investor, joined Skyroot's board as part of the deal.

The company previously made history in 2022 by launching Vikram-S, India's first privately built rocket to reach space. It now operates four facilities in Hyderabad, including its new Infinity campus capable of building one rocket per month.

## Why This Matters for the Indian Diaspora

Skyroot's launch represents a significant milestone for India's ambitions to capture a larger share of the global space economy, currently estimated at over $400 billion. The company aims to provide affordable, dedicated launch services for the small satellite market — a segment with rapidly growing demand.

AK Bhatt, Director General of the Indian Space Association, called the achievement "a defining moment for the country's private space ecosystem" and a signal to global investors that India has built a credible, innovation-driven space industry.

For Indian-origin professionals and investors in Silicon Valley and beyond, Skyroot's trajectory mirrors the kind of deep-tech entrepreneurship that has long been dominated by U.S. companies like Rocket Lab and Firefly Aerospace.
